content: The North Hampshire Hospital, previously known as Basingstoke District Hospital, is a National Health Service (NHS) hospital located in Basingstoke, Hampshire, England. It has a capacity of 400 beds and operates under the Basingstoke and North Hampshire NHS Foundation Trust. As of 2006, the hospital employed approximately 3,000 staff members and provided care to 180,000 patients annually. In 1999, this hospital became the first in Europe to perform surgical procedures using equipment controlled by voice commands. In 2002, the hospital inaugurated a new Postgraduate Medical Centre known as The Ark Centre. This facility is an independent charity located on the hospital campus and is managed by the North Hampshire Medical Education Trust, a registered charity. The Ark Centre collaborates with the hospital to deliver a variety of postgraduate educational programs and also functions as an independent conference center. The Ark Centre works in partnership with other organizations, including the Pelican Cancer Foundation, a charity focused on curing pelvic and liver cancers through precision surgical techniques, and Southampton University’s nurse training facility. The Ark Centre is particularly known for hosting advanced technological conferences, including medical and surgical meetings, and is equipped with state-of-the-art IT systems and interactive live case presentation capabilities. Additionally, the charity supports numerous community activities, such as educational and self-help meetings, which are held within the Ark Centre. The hospital has also served as a filming location for both series of the Channel 4 comedy show Green Wing. Within the hospital grounds, there is a children’s play area featuring an elephant-shaped fountain created by sculptor Sioban Coppinger, located in Hunters Courtyard. Furthermore, the hospital operates its own radio station, Hospital Radio Basingstoke, which broadcasts on 945 kHz AM and is also accessible on channel 6 through the bedside PatientLine units.
